claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about Child Benefit for Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now, let me ask you the first key question: **Do you live in the UK, and do you live with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. But no, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep.

**Are you currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's care, such as money for food, clothes, pocket money, or housing costs?** If so, could you tell me roughly how much you contribute and how often?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards Alex's upkeep. I help with things like clothes, school supplies, and other essentials. I give about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Now, I need to check an important detail: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you the only person who could potentially claim for them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex. I'm the only one who could claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: **How long has Alex been living away from you? Specifically, when did Alex move to live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been living away from me for a while now - they've been with their other parent for about the past year or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

Just to clarify one more thing: **Your weekly contributions of £30 towards Alex's upkeep - have you been making these contributions consistently throughout the year that Alex has been living with their other parent, or did they start at a different time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I've been making the £30 weekly contributions consistently throughout this time. I've kept up with supporting Alex even though they're not living with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me work through the rules:

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can normally get Child Benefit for **8 weeks after the child goes to live with someone else**. However, this can continue for longer if you make contributions to your child's upkeep.

In your case:
- Alex has been living with their other parent for about a year
- You have been making consistent weekly contributions of £30 towards Alex's upkeep (clothes, school supplies, and other essentials)
- You are the only person claiming for Alex
- The current Child Benefit rate is £24.50 per week for the first child

Since your weekly contributions of £30 exceed the Child Benefit payment amount of £24.50 per week, and you've been making these contributions consistently throughout the year, you meet the criteria for continuing to receive Child Benefit beyond the initial 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Your consistent weekly contributions of £30 towards Alex's upkeep exceed the Child Benefit payment rate, which means you can continue to claim beyond the initial 8-week period. Since you're the only person claiming for Alex, you meet all the eligibility criteria.

If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim for Child Benefit through the usual application process. If you need to provide evidence of your contributions to HMRC, keep records of your payments to show they've been made consistently.
